research.ember_notes.desc: The mechanical research bench carves an ember note out of dawnstone and computation data; obtaining the note unlocks Ember tech.
research.radiance_notes.desc: With the ember note as its draft, the mechanical bench records the observation and resonance of starlight; obtaining the note unlocks Starlight tech.
research.node.notes_primitive.name: Kinetic: The First Note
research.notes_primitive.desc: The primitive research table grinds paper and ink sac into your first research note; being able to write it down and repeat it is what opens the kinetic age.
research.node.blueprint_mechanical.name: Steam: Mechanical Blueprint
research.blueprint_mechanical.desc: The mechanical research bench turns a blank blueprint into the mechanical blueprint: machinery now has drawings to follow, and steam (steel) opens with it.
research.electric_notes.desc: The mechanical research bench carves the electric note out of wafer elements and computation data: 8 elements, 16 computation data and one paper, 900 seconds. Obtaining the note unlocks the Basic Electric Age, opening AE2 itself and Industrial Foregoing.
jei.sinkjourney.mechanical_lab.info: The stage-two bench: its west face takes a stress input interface (32 RPM minimum) and turns research notes from the primitive table into computation data, engraving the Mechanical blueprint. A hollow 3x3x3 brass shell with four upgrade slots; before the electric era there is no FE, so it runs purely on Create rotational stress.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_nexus.info: Engraves blueprints: feed blank blueprints, computation data and era materials, then spend FE. Upgrade modules can be installed on all four sides; the level slot decides which era can be engraved.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_compute.info: The CPU of the array: continuously consumes research substrate and water while venting steam. That steam must be reclaimed by the cooling core, otherwise backed-up outputs stall the computation.
jei.sinkjourney.trace_cooling.info: Continuously draws off the steam vented by the computation core and dissipates it as heat. It needs constant power; without it steam backs up and the CPU stops.
jei.sinkjourney.primitive_research.info: The primitive research table: the only research device before the stress era. Right-click to open its UI, put the materials into the two input slots (paper + ink sac, or research notes x4 + paper), and the machine starts on its own; when the bar fills the product moves to the output slot on the right.
jei.sinkjourney.primitive_research.info2: Recipes: paper + ink sac -> research notes x2 (5 min); research notes x4 + paper -> primitive blueprint (5 min). Research notes are the entry material for the mechanical research bench.
jei.sinkjourney.primitive_research.info3: Why: recording and reproducing are two different kinds of labour. First ink turns observations into notes, then several notes are compared and copied into a blueprint. With no machinery in the primitive era everything is done by hand, so every recipe takes 5 minutes. The UI has a minesweeper entry: clearing one round advances the current progress by 50%.
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info: A 3x3x3 brick-built charcoal furnace: crushed silver/gold and the electrum alloy can only be smelted here. Fuel goes into the input slots of the machine UI; any coal or charcoal works (minecraft:coals).
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info2: Build: a 3x3x3 brick shell with the controller block in the middle of the front face; a lit campfire sits at the very heart of the furnace (directly behind the controller) with a one-block flue left open at the top centre so you can see the flame. The controller has its own input/output slots, no extra hatches needed. Dousing the fire halts the furnace; an atmospheric bellows attached anywhere to the furnace shell speeds it up by 20%.
jei.kubejs.charcoal_furnace.info3: Pyres cannot touch precious metals: crushed silver/gold have no pyre recipe at all; their reducing smelt belongs to the charcoal furnace only.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info: A 3x3x4 mud-brick earthen blast furnace: the dedicated iron reduction furnace. Crushed iron x2 + calcite x1 + coal/charcoal x2 -> iron ingot x2, 70s per batch. Vanilla smelting of iron ore, raw iron and iron dust has been removed.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info2: Build: a 3x3x4 mud-brick shell with one electrum block in the middle of the bottom front row (the tuyere) and the controller block directly above it; everything else is mud bricks. A lit campfire sits at the heart (directly behind the controller), and the two-block flue above it must reach the sky. The controller has its own input/output slots, no extra hatches needed.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info3: Forced draft: an atmospheric bellows must be attached to the lower half of the shell (at or below tuyere height), otherwise the machine will not start. Dousing the campfire also halts it.
jei.kubejs.earth_blast_furnace.info4: Why: under forced draft the coal burns to CO first, and CO reduces the iron oxides; the calcite decomposes into CaO, which fluxes the silica/alumina gangue into slag, protecting the lining and cutting iron loss. Puddling/forging is abstracted away, so the furnace taps usable iron ingots directly.

research.node.ember_notes.name: Ember: Heat Cycle Notes
research.node.radiance_notes.name: Starlight: Resonance Notes
research.node.electric_notes.name: Electric: Basic Notes

research.node.electric_grid.name: Electric: Grid Dispatch
research.end_door.desc: Write the readings down the first time you step into the End: the far side of the door is research material in itself.
research.electric_winding.desc: Tabulate turns, wire gauge and flux for the windings so electric machines no longer have to be guessed at.
research.electric_grid.desc: Study how generators and loads dispatch against each other so the grid can run at full load without tripping.
research.gate_dragon.desc: Kill the ender dragon to prove this production line can carry an expedition into the End; the End gate opens (unlocks gate.end).
jei.kubejs.chemical_reactor.tiers: Six tiers differ only in structure and ports: Kinetic 3x3x4 (kinetic hatches + small energy, 1 parallel), Steam 3x3x4 (steam + normal, 2), IU Basic 3x3x5 (basic + reinforced, 2), IU Improved 3x3x5 (improved + big, 4), IU Advanced 3x3x6 (advanced + huge, 6), IU Perfect 3x3x7 (perfect + ludicrous, 8). Hatches from another tier will not form the machine.
jei.kubejs.chemical_reactor.info: Chemical reactor: trichlorosilane disproportionates into silane plus silicon tetrachloride (4SiHCl3 -> SiH4 + 3SiCl4), and silicon tetrachloride plus hydrogen returns trichlorosilane and hydrochloric acid, closing the chlorine loop.
jei.kubejs.chemical_reactor.info2: All six share one recipe pool, so upgrading only swaps the machine: same feedstock, more parallel batches and larger hatches. Disproportionation eats 4000 mB of trichlorosilane per batch, so 8-way parallel needs 32000 mB and therefore the top IU-grade hatches. IU's gas combiner, fluid/solid/triple-solid reactors, liquid integrator and polymerizer pools are banned outright and their recipes live here; solid products need an item output bus on the west wall of layer y2.
jei.kubejs.chemical_reactor.mechanics: The kettle's three mechanics ports sit on the south wall: a pneumatic interface (pressurised liquid-phase reactions: polymerisation at 5 bar, hydrogenation and chlorine recovery at 10 bar), an agitator slot (paddle, turbine, ribbon; viscous polymerisation and mixed-acid nitration need a turbine), and a lining slot (glass, stainless, titanium; sulfuric acid leaching wants glass, mixed acid wants stainless, chlorine service and HF want titanium). All three blocks must be placed for the machine to form, and a recipe whose grade does not match stays blocked.
jei.kubejs.column_reactor.info: Universal column reactor: 3x3x8, stainless steel shell. Two process pools: counter-current absorption (SO3 absorption, nitric acid absorption, HCl absorption) and reactive distillation (trichlorosilane disproportionation). Gas enters at the bottom, liquid at the top; bottoms leave low, off-gas leaves high.
jei.kubejs.column_reactor.pools: The tray slot (steel, stainless, inconel, titanium) sets absorption efficiency and speed; the resin slot (gel, macroporous) only matters for reactive distillation. Disproportionation moved here from the kettle because that is what it is in reality: a catalytic distillation column.
research.node.mid_pgm.name: Midgame: Platinum Group
research.mid_pgm.desc: Plain nickel does not need this: only platinum-group metals justify feeding a whole stack of nickel concentrate into the heat centrifuge, trading heat and yield for one platinum and one palladium. Obtaining the first platinum records era.mid.
research.node.mid_re.name: Midgame: Rare Earths
research.mid_re.desc: Rare earth hydrometallurgy: 4 purified crushed rare earth ores float into 1 concentrate; caustic cracking, oxidation roasting and a selective hydrochloric leach strip the cerium first, then P204 splits light from middle-heavy, P507 splits La, Pr-Nd, Gd and Y, oxalate precipitation and calcination give the oxides, fluorination and calciothermic reduction give the metal, and the electric furnace casts it. Obtaining the first neodymium records the rare earth milestone (era.mid_re).
jei.kubejs.nc_chem_reactor.info: The NuclearCraft hot-cell processing cell is the batch dissolver/fluorinator of a reprocessing plant, not a general reactor: fuel dissolution, fluoride volatilisation and reprocessing, plus molten-salt solvents, coolants and boron/barium auxiliaries. It is highly radioactive, works in small batches and never runs in parallel - build more cells rather than a bigger one. Bulk chemistry (methanol, sulfuric acid, SO2 oxidation) belongs to this pack's MMCR reactors, which carry tiered internals, pressure gates and parallelism, so no reaction runs here twice.
jei.kubejs.litho_mk1.info: Mercury g-line 436 nm / NA 0.28. Single exposure resolves about 700 nm, so it takes only M1 1.5um and M2 800nm reticles.
jei.kubejs.litho_mk2.info: Mercury i-line 365 nm / NA 0.55. Single exposure around 300 nm, enough for M3 350nm.
jei.kubejs.litho_mk3.info: KrF excimer 248 nm / NA 0.70. Single exposure around 160 nm, good for M4 180nm and nothing finer.
machine.sinkjourney.litho_mk4: ArF Immersion Lithography Machine Mk.IV (193 nm)
recipe_pool.sinkjourney.litho_mk4: ArF Immersion Lithography Machine Mk.IV (193 nm)
jei.kubejs.litho_mk4.info: ArF excimer 193 nm / NA 1.35 with water immersion. Single exposure around 64 nm, so M5 90nm fits; M6 28nm needs double patterning and two doses of resist and developer.
jei.kubejs.litho_common.info: All three lithography steps live in this machine: coat (photoresist), expose (reticle plus projection optics), develop (250 mB of NaOH developer). Projection optics are installed hardware and are not consumed; reticles wear at 0.1% per wafer.
jei.kubejs.photoresist.info: Photoresist: the real thing is novolak resin plus a diazonaphthoquinone sensitiser, approximated here with plastic and redstone. One sheet per exposure, two for double patterning.
jei.kubejs.optics.info: Pick projection optics by the shortest wavelength they transmit: UV glass stops at 436 nm (g-line), fused silica at 240 nm (i-line and KrF), calcium fluoride at 150 nm, and the immersion lens set only fits ArF. They stay installed, so changing wavelength means changing optics.
jei.kubejs.universal_reactor.info: Universal reactor: 3x3x6, inconel shell. One machine carries four process pools: fixed bed (steam reforming, CO shift, SO2 oxidation, ammonia oxidation, naphtha hydrotreating), fluidized bed (chlorination, cold hydrogenation), high pressure (methanol, ammonia synthesis) and tubular cracking (naphtha cracking). Pick the pool in the controller; JEI shows only that pool.
jei.kubejs.universal_reactor.pools: Feedstock enters west, north and east; products leave one layer up; the item ports take powder, catalyst and petroleum coke. Three internals: catalyst (nickel, iron-chromia, copper-zinc/vanadia, promoted iron, platinum-rhodium), pressure vessel (forged, multilayer, wire-wound) and furnace tube (steel, molybdenum, inconel, titanium; cracking only). All three must hold a block for the machine to form; put the lowest grade in the slot you are not using.
jei.kubejs.universal_reactor.catalyst: Pressure gates use PneumaticCraft: 2 bar for hydrotreating and cracking, 3 bar for reforming, 20 bar for methanol and ammonia synthesis (the compressor ceiling; the real processes run at 5-30 MPa, abstracted through pressure vessel grades). The heat-input hatch sits in the structure but no recipe requires it yet.
jei.kubejs.large_reactor.info: Large universal reactor: 5x5x7-9, three grades stainless, titanium and cobalt-chrome, 8/10/12 parallels, hatches locked to the matching grade. Same four pools as the standard machine, with ports sized for bulk and multi-stream work: four fluid inputs, five fluid outputs, two item ports, so the five cracking cuts each get their own line.
jei.kubejs.large_reactor.ports: The three internals are unchanged. Two energy hatches plus a heat input and a heat output suit a train that still dumps heat to a boiler. Every grade raises shell, hatch tier and height together, so upgrading is a material and capacity step, not just a number.
jei.kubejs.large_column.info: Large column reactor: 5x5x9-11, three grades inconel, titanium and cobalt-chrome, 3/4/6 parallels, hatches locked to the grade. Two tray slots split the tower so absorption and rectification can run in one shell; two feed lines each for gas and liquid, three bottoms outlets. Put the same tray grade in both slots to avoid ambiguity.
jei.kubejs.rare_earth_concentrate.info: Rare Earth Concentrate: 4 monazite float into 1 concentrate (about 60% REO). Real monazite carries cerium, lanthanum, neodymium, gadolinium and yttrium in one ore - the elements only separate in the extraction stage, so the pack has one rare earth ore and one concentrate.
jei.kubejs.monazite.info: Monazite: (Ce,La,Nd)PO4, a rare earth phosphate. Feed of the rare earth hydrometallurgy line; 4 monazite float into 1 concentrate, and one ore carries cerium, lanthanum, neodymium, gadolinium and yttrium at once.
jei.kubejs.monazite_ore.info: Monazite Ore (Mars): a rare earth phosphate deposit, dropping 2 monazite per block. Real rare earths are never mined as single-element ores - the elements split in the extraction stage, so Mars carries only this one rare earth ore.
jei.kubejs.rare_earth_concentrate.steps: Downstream: caustic cracking -> oxidation roast (cerium to Ce(IV)) -> hydrochloric selective leach, cerium stays in the residue -> neutralisation -> P204 light/middle-heavy split -> P507 splits La, Pr-Nd, Gd, Y -> oxalate precipitation and calcination -> fluorination -> calciothermic reduction -> rare earth powder -> electric furnace casting. Per concentrate: Nd 1, Gd 0.25, Y 0.25, La2O3 0.5, CeO2 0.5.
jei.kubejs.rare_earth_ingot.info: Rare earth ingots only come from the hydrometallurgical line: ore and purified crushed ore can no longer be smelted into ingots, and the centrifuge no longer yields rare earth dust. Oxide -> fluoride -> calciothermic reduction -> powder -> electric furnace. Rare earth oxides are far too stable for carbon reduction; the metal comes from fluoride calciothermic reduction or molten salt electrolysis.
jei.kubejs.cerium_rich_residue.info: Cerium-rich residue: after the oxidation roast turns Ce(III) into Ce(IV), CeO2 does not dissolve in hydrochloric acid, so cerium stays in this residue during the selective leach - that is where cerium is first separated, not in the extractors. Nitric acid dissolution, oxalate precipitation and calcination give cerium oxide.
jei.kubejs.iron_thorium_residue.info: Iron-thorium residue: the insoluble part of neutralisation and cerium dissolution, carrying iron, thorium and gangue. Thorium is a naturally occurring radioactive companion of rare earth ores and the heaviest environmental cost of the industry; store it safely.
jei.kubejs.prnd_oxide.info: Praseodymium-neodymium oxide: a mixed oxide of Pr6O11 and Nd2O3. The Pr/Nd separation factor is only about 1.5, so industry runs hundreds of extraction stages or simply sells Pr-Nd alloy - the neodymium ingot in this pack is that Pr-Nd metal.
block.nuclearcraftneohaul.chemical_react: A sealed batch cell for dissolving fuel, volatilising fluorides and mixing salt solvents. Highly radioactive, small batches, no parallelism: build more cells instead of a bigger one.
research.node.improved_notes.name: Electric: Improved Casings and Molybdenum
research.improved_notes.desc: Stainless 304 gets you in; only the hydrogen reduction of molybdenum and the 316L charge make the improved machines placeable.
